record.original_question: Let ABC be a triangle and P an interior point. Let P(A), P(B), and P(C) be the intersections of the cevians AP, BP, and CP with the side lines BC, CA, and AB, respectively. Erect perpendiculars to BC, CA, and AB at P(A), P(B), and P(C), and define P(*) when those three perpendiculars are concurrent. For standard triangle centers such as the centroid, circumcenter, incenter, orthocenter, Gergonne point, and Nagel point, determine the analogues for P(*) of the existence and identification questions asked for P*.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let ABC be a triangle in the Euclidean plane and let P be an interior point. Define the cevian traces
- P_A = AP ∩ BC,
- P_B = BP ∩ CA,
- P_C = CP ∩ AB.

At each trace erect the line perpendicular to the corresponding side of the triangle: let ℓ_A be the line through P_A perpendicular to BC, ℓ_B the line through P_B perpendicular to CA, and ℓ_C the line through P_C perpendicular to AB. When the three perpendiculars ℓ_A, ℓ_B, ℓ_C are concurrent, denote their common point by P^*; in this case call P "dual-perpendicular admissible" and call P^* the dual-perpendicular companion of P.

Investigate the following for each of the classical triangle centers P ∈ {centroid G, circumcenter O, incenter I, orthocenter H, Gergonne point Ge, Nagel point Na}:

(a) Determine whether P is dual-perpendicular admissible for every triangle ABC (i.e., whether ℓ_A, ℓ_B, ℓ_C are always concurrent for that choice of P). If admissibility holds only on a proper subfamily of triangles, characterize that subfamily.

(b) When P^* exists, identify the point P^* as a named triangle center (or give explicit barycentric/trilinear coordinates for P^* in terms of the side lengths a, b, c of ABC).

(c) Describe the locus of points P in the interior of ABC for which the three perpendiculars ℓ_A, ℓ_B, ℓ_C are concurrent, and describe the map P ↦ P^* on this locus.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for the dual-perpendicular concurrence construction associated with the listed classical triangle centers did not turn up published resolutions identifying the resulting points P^* or characterizing the admissible locus for centroid, circumcenter, incenter, orthocenter, Gergonne, and Nagel points in this specific dual form. Standard references discuss the orthocenter case (P = orthocenter trivially yields concurrence via the altitudes) but a complete treatment for all six centers in the dual-perpendicular setting was not located, so the overall status is taken as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Concurrence of perpendicular bisectors of a triangle
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference on perpendicular concurrence in a triangle; does not address the dual-perpendicular companion problem for the listed centers.
status_evidence.claim: Background on perpendicular concurrences exists but the specific dual problem is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Introduction to the Geometry of the Triangle (Yiu)
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive treatment of triangle centers and cevian constructions in barycentric coordinates.
status_evidence.claim: While related cevian and perpendicular constructions are catalogued, the dual-perpendicular companions of G, O, I, H, Ge, Na are not given an explicit unified resolution.
